sites.period: house of C17 date on internal evidence, core possibly medieval; altered C19; demolished 6 Dec 1988; first found mention by name 1824
sites.confidence: medium-high: Stewart 1824 plan homestead group (tithe 1841 plots 209/210 'Courtyard &c', traced) centroid ST 16737 73353 agrees within c. 30 m with HER 02038s NGR ST16707335. Coflein 20182 gives ST1681073310 (c. 85 m east) — differing record
known: limestone (local lias) house and barn next to the parish church (HER 02038s)
cross-passage, end-chimney plan with masonry partitions and battered N wall; ogee-stopped beams (Suggett/RCAHMW 1988)
estimated: building sizes and pitches from Tŷ Mawr reference photographs (4 Nov 2026) and two reference paintings and a historic aerial photograph (5 Nov 2026) (tools/tymawr-layout.json, 'best guess')

layout (v0.2.0, corrected 5 Nov 2026): the house and the stable range face south, with the stable front level with the house front (not forward of it); the stone barn on the west side of the group runs north-south and faces west, with the stable range joined at its south-east corner; distances between the barn group and the house, wall and lane lines, the glasshouse and the gate tree are estimated

church shown as massing only (v0.2.1): position from the OSM church point, c.107 m SE of the pin, as HER 02038s and the 1824 Stewart plan place it; a historic aerial photograph (5 Nov 2026) shows the tower east of the house group; the earlier photo-scaled geometry had placed it NE

lane (v0.2.1): drawn as a semicircle around the church, between the church and the house and its buildings, which sit on the outside of the curve; radius about 74 m, estimated; meadow hedges and the track north from a painted aerial plan, positions not checked
